overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: minutes were approved on time and posting is not required. An unclear minutes-request claim was not reviewed, and the Board was reminded of the 10-day availability rule.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board had not made minutes public or posted them since July 2024, implying untimely approval of minutes.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board created and approved minutes of meetings held between August 19, 2024, and October 7, 2024, within the timeframe required by the Open Meeting Law, that is, within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued meeting minutes should have been posted to the municipal website.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require public bodies to post meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant asserted he requested minutes from the Board and was not provided them.
allegations.key_passage: we find that this allegation was not clearly raised in the complaint and thus we do not review its merits.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
